title: CBP provides a base of operations for FEMA INTF-1 for Hurricane Florence operations
description: CBP Port Director Scott Opalka and FEMA Indiana Task Force 1 Rescue Squad Officer Pedro Caceres discuss the cooperation between CBP and FEMA during the federal response to Hurricane Florence.  U.S. Customs and Border Protection facilitated an operations base for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Indiana Task Force 1 (INTF-1) at CBP’s facility in the Wilmington International Airport, Wilmington, NC.  INTF-1 has been conducting search and rescue operations and restoration of transportation routes since arriving on September 12, 2018.  Video produced by George Felton -  September 15, 2018.

transcript.text: - I received a request from New Hanover
Emergency Operation Center
and they requested that we see if we had space
to host a task force from Indiana.
Due to the nature of the storm,
we agreed to open our facility
to help them stage and conduct search
and rescues in the community.
- Working with the CBP here has been fantastic.
There's only 2% out so far here from their team.
I understand there's more on their way
but the two that are here have gone way out of their way
to provide everything we need.
- [Scott] A staging area like this is very important.
It give the responders a nice, safe, secure environment.
So they can go out, conduct their operations,
come back, rest up, and go back out the next day.
The partnership was being by a signal.
They are one of the DHS components.
So we are more than happy to support whether it's FEMA main
or one of their task forces to come in.
We're all here to help the community,
that is our number one priority.
